subject: Plain-language FAQ: subprocessors & cross-border transfers for Hosted API console
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@cyclone.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick ask: public-friendly text about your subprocessors and transfers

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the throughput numbers look promising. Legal is asking for a single-page, consumer-friendly explanation we can share internally that covers: who your subprocessors are (high level), what kinds of data leave the EU (if any), and what safeguards you apply for cross-border transfers.

They said the standard DPA language is fine for contracts, but they need something shorter and plain for non-legal stakeholders and for inclusion in our vendor review packet. Can you send a short draft or point us to a one-pager?

Thanks,
Olivia
Senior Procurement Manager
Cyclone AI

[Attachment: procurement_template.xlsx]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@cyclone.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: public-friendly text about your subprocessors and transfers

Hi Olivia — great question and totally reasonable. I attached a short draft one-pager and a two-paragraph blurb we use in the console. Key points up front:

- We publish a high-level list of subprocessors (storage, telemetry, compute) and keep the list up to date.
- For hosted API customers, data used for inference may transit geographically for routing or caching; we provide residency controls on dedicated/private plans.
- Cross-border transfers: we rely on standard safeguards (SCCs or equivalent) and selective pseudonymization for telemetry; more details in the DPA.

Can @Laura and @Kimberly take a quick look for legal tone and anything we should avoid saying publicly? Olivia, I kept the language focused and non-technical — feel free to mark anything you want tightened for your packet.

Thanks,
Rishi
Account Executive — North America
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_onepager_v1.docx, data_flow_summary_for_sales.pdf]

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, olivia@cyclone.ai
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>, vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: public-friendly text about your subprocessors and transfers

Thanks Rishi — good start. I made a few small edits to tighten accuracy and reduce implied guarantees:

- Replace "data used for inference may transit geographically" with "requests and limited, transient metadata may be routed across regions to optimize latency; customers can opt for regional routing on Dedicated and Private plans."
- Add: "We do not use customer inputs to train our public models unless a customer opts in." That one is high priority for sales-facing copy.
- Clarify safeguards: "We rely on contractual safeguards (SCCs), Encryption in transit and at rest, and strict access controls; detailed measures are in the DPA and security whitepaper."

Kimberly — can you confirm the phrasing on SCCs and the training line? Vanessa — please add any console copy constraints (length, preferred tone).

Laura Bennett
Head of Product Marketing
Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.inference>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.inference>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.inference>, olivia@cyclone.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick ask: public-friendly text about your subprocessors and transfers

Looks good — approved with one tweak for consumer-facing simplicity: shorten the lead paragraph and add a two-sentence FAQ at the bottom that answers: "Will my data be used to improve models?" and "How do I request data residency?"

Suggested FAQ lines (two bullets):
- "We do not use your API inputs to train our public models unless you explicitly opt in via the service agreement or console setting."
- "To request a regional residency option, contact your account rep or enable it in Dedicated/Private plan settings; small customers can request help via support."

Olivia — if that covers Legal's needs we can push the one-pager and the console blurb to our shared Drive and add a short help center link for your vendor packet.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
